The writ petition is preferred by a company which is involved in marketing, distributing and selling all over India of branded product called 'Beco Special'.
It is stated that the said product is a food or nutritional supplement manufactured under valid license issued by the statutory authorities.

The grievance voiced in this writ petition is that Ext.P3 prosecution initiated by the 1st respondent on the premise that the said product was made without availing a valid drug manufacturing license.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner Company is manufacturing and marketing a range of pharmaceutical products and food or nutritional supplements.

In this case the petitioner is selling a branded product named 4 2024:KER:75200 'Beco Special' all over India including State of Kerala, which is a food or nutritional supplement manufactured by M/s. Geltec Private Limited,
Mumbai under the PFA license issued by the Government of Karnataka under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
The said product is a nutritional supplement and not a drug, and its wrapper, package and literature clearly say that it is a nutritional or food supplement.
The product complies with the standards prescribed for food supplements under the Nutrient Requirement and Recommended Dietary Allowance for Indians as issued by ICMR.

3. It is further stated that the said product is not covered by the definition of 'drug' as defined in M/S.Pfizer Limited vs The Drugs Inspector on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83933381/
2 Section 3(b) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, as the same is not a medicine or drug intended for internal or external use of human beings or animals.

sentences.text: The said product is not used for therapeutical purpose also, as the same is a dietary supplement.
While so, they received a communication as per Ext.P1 stating that the 1st respondent has initiated prosecution against the company in respect of 'Beco Special' marketed by the petitioner.
It is for the reason that the petitioner had manufactured and marketed drugs under the guise of food supplements without a 5 2024:KER:75200 valid drug manufacturing license to do so.
It was instructed the petitioner to produce certain documents as per Ext.P3.

The writ petition is preferred stating that the 1st respondent has no jurisdiction to issue Ext.P3, as the same does not come within the definition of Section 3(b) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.

4. When the matter is taken up for consideration today, the learned Government Pleader as well as the petitioner, brought to my notice a judgment dated 06.01.2014 in W.P.(C) No.30667 of 2010 and connected matters, wherein by paragraphs 4 and 5 the judgment the entire issue has been dealt with in detail.
For the purpose of convenience, para 4 and 5 reproduced herein below:
"4. DC Act defines 'drug'.
It also prescribes standards for various drugs, also through Rules, Schedules etc. and also through notifications thereunder.
There could also be drugs, for which no standards are prescribed.
But, a survey of the provisions of that Act would show that the liability that a person who violates provisions of DC Act and the Rules thereunder would incur is criminal liability.
The process is initiated on the strength of materials generated by way of search, seizure etc. or by other modes noticing actions in violation of 6 2024:KER:75200 DC Act and Rules thereunder.
The Government Analyst is the authority to certify the nature of the materials.

This means that the Government Analyst has the power to decide as to whether a particular material is a drug in terms of the DC Act and if it is so, as to whether any particular standard is prescribed for the said drug and whether the sample conforms to such prescriptions.
The statute has provided conclusiveness for the certificate that would be issued by the Government Analyst.
Such material would be fundamental when prosecution is initiated by making complaint before the competent Magistrate in terms of the provisions of the DC Act.
The authority to make a complaint is with the competent officer in that regard.

We do not see any other provisions in the DC Act which enables any other mode to provide a different platform for the manufacturer,
distributor, dealer, supplier etc., to demonstrate his innocence or to have a consideration as to whether a substance that is being sold by him is drug as per DC Act and the Rules and notifications thereunder, or not.

5. For the aforesaid reasons, these petitions are ordered recording that the orders which are impugned in some of the writ petitions have worked themselves out by efflux of time, even according to the Inspectors and that the learned senior government pleader has submitted on behalf of the State that there will be no oral 7 2024:KER:75200 instructions or directions being issued against transactions.

This means that the State and the Inspectors under the DC Act are duty bound to ensure that the rights of citizens are appropriately protected by taking due action in strict conformity with the provisions of that Act and the Rules and notifications thereunder and they M/S.Pfizer Limited vs The Drugs Inspector on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83933381/
3 would have no choice but to go for prosecution if a case is made out regarding commission of offence in terms of that Act, Rules or notifications".

sentences.text: 5. It is concluded that there is no effective mechanism to assess the nature of the product.
It could be decided after initiating prosecution.
Then the sample will be taken and sent to the analyst during the prosecution.
On obtaining such a report from the analyst, it can be decided that the product in question is a drug or other food supplement.
Only thereafter the innocence of the said party can be ascertained.
6. Under such circumstances, it is desirable to direct the petitioner to face the prosecution with respect to the alleged commission of offence, if any, in terms of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
In the light of said direction in Ext.R1(a) judgment, this writ petition is closed with a direction to the petitioner Company to follow the directions in the said judgment and face the prosecution.
The writ petition is disposed of as above.
